`edit`: a simple text editor, after nano.

## Synopsis

<strong>edit</strong> \[<em>file</em>\]

## Description

<strong>edit</strong> is a full-screen text editor, in the style of <strong>nano</strong>. It shows a title bar (with the file's name, and <strong>Modified</strong> once it has changed), the text, a status line, and two lines of shortcuts.

It opens <em>file</em> if it exists, and says <strong>\[ New File \]</strong> if not; with no <em>file</em> it starts an empty buffer, and asks for a name when it is written out.

Typing inserts text at the cursor; Tab inserts two spaces. A line too long for the terminal scrolls sideways on the cursor's line, with a <strong>$</strong> where it goes on past either edge.

<strong>edit</strong> runs on the terminal's alternate screen with the tty in raw mode, and puts both back however it ends.

## Keys

<strong>Arrow keys</strong>, <strong>Home</strong>, <strong>End</strong>
: Move the cursor. Left and Right go on to the next or the previous line.

<strong>PageUp</strong>, <strong>PageDown</strong>, <strong>^Y</strong>, <strong>^V</strong>
: Move a screen up or down.

<strong>^A</strong>, <strong>^E</strong>
: Go to the start or the end of the line.

<strong>Enter</strong>
: Split the line at the cursor.

<strong>Backspace</strong>, <strong>Delete</strong>
: Erase the character before or under the cursor, joining lines at either end.

<strong>^K</strong>
: Cut the cursor's line. Cuts one after another go together.

<strong>^U</strong>
: Paste the lines last cut, above the cursor's line.

<strong>^W</strong>
: Search for text (case matters), from the cursor on, wrapping round at the end. An empty answer searches for the last text again.

<strong>^C</strong>
: Show the cursor's position: line, column, and how far through the file.

<strong>^O</strong>
: Write the file out, asking for its name (the current one is offered).

<strong>^X</strong>
: Exit. With unsaved changes it asks whether to save them first: <strong>Y</strong> saves (and exits only if that worked), <strong>N</strong> throws them away, and <strong>^C</strong> cancels.

At a question on the status line, Enter answers it, Backspace erases, and <strong>^C</strong> or Escape cancels.

## Exit status

0 when it exits normally, including at the end of its input; 1 if <em>file</em> exists but cannot be read.

## Notes

A file is written with a new line after its last line; a carriage return at the end of a line is dropped when the file is read. There is no undo, no syntax highlighting, and no mouse support.

## See also

<strong>less</strong>(1), <strong>cat</strong>(1), <strong>stty</strong>(1)
